clauses.reason: Section 1 closes all Executive departments and agencies and excuses their employees from duty on Friday, December 26, 1986, the day following Christmas Day, except as Section 2 allows. The provision names December 26, 1986 alone and was performed when that day ended, so its first end is 1986-12-26, recorded inclusive (the order operates through the day; the exclusive reading, ending when the day begins, cannot apply to a command about that day). The packet lookup of held texts citing this order by number found none.

Section 2 lets the heads of Executive departments and agencies decide that certain offices and installations stay open and certain employees report for duty on December 26, 1986 for reasons of national security or defense or other public reasons. The provision names December 26, 1986 alone and was performed when that day ended, so its first end is 1986-12-26, recorded inclusive (the order operates through the day; the exclusive reading, ending when the day begins, cannot apply to a command about that day). The packet lookup of held texts citing this order by number found none.

Section 3 provides that Friday, December 26, 1986 is to be considered as falling within the scope of Executive Order No. 11582 and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and leave of employees of the United States. The provision names December 26, 1986 alone and was performed when that day ended, so its first end is 1986-12-26, recorded inclusive (the order operates through the day; the exclusive reading, ending when the day begins, cannot apply to a command about that day). The packet lookup of held texts citing this order by number found none.
